chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said to one of his slaves: 'Buy less for us from the onions, and more for us from the aubergines.' So he said to him (peace be upon him) inquiring, 'The aubergines?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, the aubergines, it gathers all tastes, removes illness, is suitable for the constitution, balanced in its states, suitable for the old man and the young man, moderate in its heat and coldness, hot in the place of heat and cold in the place of cold.'
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits and characteristics of aubergines according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam (peace be upon him) demonstrates the Shia emphasis on *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic medicine) by evaluating food through the lens of humoral balance (*Mizaj*). He praises the aubergine (*Badhinjan*) as a 'unifier of taste' and a balanced remedy, suitable for both the elderly and the young, reflecting the scholarly tradition of viewing dietary choices as integral to spiritual and physical well-being.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdul Rahman Al Hashimy who said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said to one of his slaves: ‘Be (buy) less for us<sup>asws</sup> from the onions, and more for us<sup>asws</sup> from the aubergines’. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup> for his understanding, ‘The aubergines?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, the aubergines, in all its tastes is beneficial for the illnesses, corrective for the health, balanced in its states, corrective for the old man and the youth, being moderate in its heat and its coolness, being hot in hot places and cool in cold places’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn from Muhammad from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from and ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimiy who has said the following:

“He (the Imam), Alayhi al-Salam, once said to a certain one of his servants, ‘You must bring for us less onion and more eggplant/ He inquired saying, ‘Do you mean eggplant? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, eggplant, it is wholesome in taste, removes illness, is suitable for one’s health, balanced in its condition and it is suitable for the old people. It is balancing in hot and cold seasons; it is hot in hot places and it is cool in cold places/”
